primary_claim: Per-layer steering vectors trained by gradient descent (frozen base model) on a small amount of conversational data can induce consistent assistant-like behavior (proper EOS token use, self-identification as an AI assistant) in Qwen3-4B-Base, approaching the instruction-tuned model's performance on a simplified eval, suggesting base models already contain assistant-behavior representations that post-training mostly selects rather than newly instills

effect.metric: eval score (instruction-following, helpfulness, coherence, EOS-token use) across 25 tasks, judged by Claude Haiku 4.5
effect.value: instruct vectors approach the instruction-tuned Qwen3-4B variant's score on simplified eval, primarily lagging on proper EOS-token use though far exceeding base model

stated_future_work: Try training with loss masked to only assistant-turn sections of the dataset
Test larger sequence lengths and larger models (limited to sequence length 256 by memory constraints in this work)
Train a vector across multiple models at once to test generalization to unseen models/architectures
Explore different datasets and hyperparameter tuning, given the small amount of data needed for optimal behavior
limitations_stated: Dataset was inadvertently segmented by index such that different sample-size runs saw systematically different conversation lengths/styles
Runs 4 and 11 produced gibberish output and were not evaluated
Quantitative eval scores did not always match the author's qualitative experience (e.g. run 6 subjectively outperforming run 10 despite lower score)
Limited to sequence length 256 and smaller models due to VRAM constraints (12GB RTX 4070 Super)
Did not use a stop sequence for hallucinated conversation turns because part of the goal was to test the base model's own turn-ending behavior
quote: Small vectors with minimal data being able to steer the base model into consistent assistant behavior suggests that base models already contain the representations necessary for assistant-like behavior and post-training may be less about instilling new capabilities and more about selecting and reinforcing patterns that already exist.
